analysis:
The only changed file is .github/workflows/ci.yml, and the change is CI-only. It adds 12 macOS lanes to the `route` job's `lanes` input (head lines ~53-64), each gated on a component-classifier output or a push event with a fallback to `blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-27`. The jobs test-provider (shards 1-3), test-provider-summary, test-provider-sdk, test-cluster-checks, test-cluster (1-3), test-cluster-gpu (1-2) and test-cluster-focused now take `runs-on` from `fromJSON(needs.route.outputs.routes)[...]` and gain `needs: route`. No provider runtime code changes. No change touches A-001, A-003, the WebSocket contract (TB-002), attestation (TB-009/TB-011), the prefix cache (T-041), or the fan helper (TB-010).

The security-relevant change is that PR-controlled code (recursive submodule checkout, Swift builds, test scripts) can now run on Darkbloom Sandbox macOS runners. That runner pool is partly outside the Blacksmith trust domain. The old comment said the macOS jobs were deliberately not routed and that routing was for read-only jobs.

The routing semantics live in `.github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml` and `docs/developer/build.md`, neither of which was supplied. I could not verify the following:
- Sandbox VM isolation and ephemerality, including whether a lane is granted a fresh VM per job.
- Whether any secrets or OIDC tokens can reach these lanes.
- Whether the push path (`SAVE_CACHES` true on master/dev) now writes `actions/cache` entries from a sandbox lane. That would let a compromised lane poison the .git, provider-ci-build and cluster-metadata caches that later PR and release-adjacent runs restore.
- Whether a fork-PR or an empty lane output could make `fromJSON(...)[...]` resolve to null.

Workflow permissions stay at `contents: read`, `persist-credentials: false` is kept, and actions are SHA-pinned. I identified no concrete regression in the visible lines, but cache-write trust on routed lanes is an unresolved integration question. TB-012 and TB-013 (add-on sandbox) are related only by name; I saw no link in this diff.
